text.p: France's Aerospatiale has been awarded a contract to build three weather satellites for the European Meteorological Satellite Organisation (EUMETSAT), the company said in a statement on Wednesday.
The satellites, the second generation of EUMETSAT's Meteosat series, will be launched aboard Ariane rockets from French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America starting in the year 2000.
"The satellites will supply permanent imagery of the Earth and its cloud cover, and also retransmit data collected from ground, sea-based or airborne platforms," the statement said.

"The second generation will provide the meteorological community with imagery taken at double the rate (every 15 minutes instead of every half hour), in a much larger number of spectral channels ...These increased performances will maintain Europe's position at the forefront of meteorological observation by geostationary satellites," it said.
Aerospatiale said the three satellite contract amounted to 600 million ECUs ($747.7 million).
